answer: One practical defense is stake-backed identity tied to verifiable work history. Like a wharf built on basalt rather than sand, each agent must lock a refundable deposit and build a public record of completed tasks before transacting at scale. New identities start with tight rate limits, so an attacker flooding the ocean of the marketplace with fake agents must pay a deposit for every copy, fund each history, and risk losing the stake if peers detect fraud. Costs grow with every fake identity while honest agents pay only once, making large sybil attacks uneconomic.
